texts.full_text: the Einstein–Cartan theory, also known as the Einstein–Cartan–Sciama–Kibble theory, is a classical theory of gravitation similar to general relativity. The theory was first proposed by Élie Cartan in 1922 and expounded in the following few years. Overview Einstein-Cartan theory differs from general relativity in two ways: (1) it is formulated within the framework of Riemann-Cartan geometry, which possesses a locally gauged Lorentz symmetry, while general relativity is formulated within the framework of Riemannian geometry, which does not; (2) an additional set of equations are posed that relate torsion to spin. This difference can be factored into general relativity (Einstein-Hilbert) → general relativity (Palatini) → Einstein-Cartan by first reformulating general relativity onto a Riemann-Cartan geometry, replacing the Einstein-Hilbert action over Riemannian geometry by the Palatini action over Riemann-Cartan geometry; and second, removing the zero torsion constraint from the Palatini action, which results in the additional set of equations for spin and torsion, as well as the addition of extra spin-related terms in the Einstein field equations themselves. texts.full_text: mpiled code. This package contains interfaces and classes that provide a level above those in the jdk.vm and related packages. The main purpose is to allow tools such as profilers, debuggers etc., which need more than just raw machine instructions, to obtain information about methods without going through complex processes of decompilation or analysis. The API allows access from compiled code back into the meta-level representation that was created during compilation. This means it can be used by JIT compilers to inspect their own output, debuggers and profiler tools etc., but not necessarily by application developers. The interfaces are designed with performance in mind so they should have minimal overhead. Note: This package is experimental as part of the GraalVM project (http://www.graalvm.org/) for JDK 8.
